'''Fábio Alexandre da Silva Coentrão''' ({{IPA|pt|ˈfaβju kwẽˈtɾɐ̃w}}; born 11 March 1988) is a Portuguese former professional [[association football|footballer]]. Mainly a [[left-back]], he also operated as a [[winger (association football)|winger]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/11/transfer-zone/2010/06/23/1990887/juventus-target-benfica-winger-fabio-coentrao-report|title=Juventus target Benfica winger Fabio Coentrao – Report|publisher=[[Goal (website)|Goal]]|last=Mira|first=Luís|date=23 June 2010|access-date=14 October 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tribalfootball.com/articles/blackburn-following-benfica-winger-fabio-coentrao-340221|title=Blackburn following Benfica winger Fabio Coentrao|publisher=Tribal Football|date=23 June 2010|access-date=14 October 2014}}</ref> and occasionally as a [[defensive midfielder]].

After starting playing professionally with [[Rio Ave F.C.|Rio Ave]], he signed for [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] at 19, going on to be loaned several times before becoming an important member of the first team as a left-back. He joined [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in 2011, and retired ten years later at his first club.

A [[Portugal national football team|Portugal international]] over eight years, Coentrão represented the nation in two [[FIFA World Cup|World Cups]] and [[UEFA Euro 2012|Euro 2012]].

==Club career==
===Rio Ave===
Born in [[Vila do Conde]], Coentrão grew up in the [[Caxinas]] fishing neighbourhood, as did his long-time international teammates [[Bruno Alves]] and [[Hélder Postiga]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://observador.pt/2017/10/27/coentrao-e-o-regresso-do-menino-querido-das-caxinas-que-seria-pescador-se-nao-fosse-o-futebol/|title=Coentrão e o regresso do menino querido das Caxinas que seria pescador se não fosse o futebol|trans-title=Coentrão and the return of Caxinas' beloved boy who would be a fisherman if it were not for football|newspaper=[[Observador]]|last=Roseiro|first=Bruno|language=pt|date=27 October 2011|access-date=26 September 2019}}</ref> He joined his hometown's [[Rio Ave F.C.]] in 2004 at the age of 16, playing three [[Primeira Liga]] games in [[2005–06 Primeira Liga|the following season]] for a northern side that would be relegated.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.record.xl.pt/Futebol/Nacional/1a_liga/rio_ave/interior.aspx?content_id=250734|title=Fábio Coentrão: "Pena ter sido tão pouco tempo"|trans-title=Fábio Coentrão: "Too bad it was so little time"|newspaper=[[Record (Portuguese newspaper)|Record]]|last=Leal|first=Luís|language=pt|date=18 October 2005|access-date=30 May 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140531104800/http://www.record.xl.pt/Futebol/Nacional/1a_liga/rio_ave/interior.aspx?content_id=250734|archive-date=31 May 2014}}</ref> In [[2006–07 Liga de Honra|2006–07]] he established himself as first-choice, as Rio Ave barely missed promotion back and had [[2006–07 Taça de Portugal|a good run]] in the [[Taça de Portugal]], ended by [[Sporting CP]] with a 2–1 win in [[Lisbon]];<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.cmjornal.pt/cm-ao-minuto/detalhe/sporting-segue-em-frente-na-taca|title=Sporting segue em frente na Taça|trans-title=Sporting go through in Cup|newspaper=[[Correio da Manhã (Portugal)|Correio da Manhã]]|language=pt|date=21 January 2007|access-date=7 April 2018}}</ref> whilst playing for the club, he earned the nickname "[[Luís Figo|Figo]] das Caxinas".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://desporto.sapo.pt/futebol/primeira-liga/artigos/coentrao-a-redencao-do-figo-de-caxinas|title=Coentrão, a redenção do "Figo de Caxinas"|trans-title=Coentrão, the redemption of the "Figo from Caxinas"|publisher=[[SAPO (company)|SAPO]]|last=Godinho|first=João Paulo|language=pt|date=10 May 2010|access-date=7 April 2018}}</ref>

After that season, where he was voted the divisions' Breakthrough Player of the Year,<ref>[http://redvermelho.blogspot.com/2007/06/simo-sabrosa-o-melhor-jogador-da-liga.html Simão Sabrosa – O Melhor Jogador da Liga Bwin 2006/2007 (Simão Sabrosa – Bwin League 2006/2007's Best Player)]; Red Vermelho, 6 Junho 2007 (in Portuguese)</ref> many clubs showed interest in Coentrão, most notably Sporting and [[S.L. Benfica]], with him choosing the latter in July 2007. His playing style was likened to that of [[Arjen Robben]] by ''[[World Soccer Magazine]]'', in its ''50 World Talents'' 2007 issue.

===Benfica===
On 1 January 2008, having received insignificant playing opportunities at Benfica, Coentrão joined [[Madeira]]'s [[C.D. Nacional]] on loan until the end of [[2007–08 Primeira Liga|the season]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.record.xl.pt/Futebol/Nacional/1a_liga/Nacional/interior.aspx?content_id=328030|title=Fábio Coentrão já trabalhou na Madeira|trans-title=Fábio Coentrão already working in Madeira|newspaper=Record|last=Avelãs|first=Luís|language=pt|date=2 January 2008|access-date=30 May 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140531090734/http://www.record.xl.pt/Futebol/Nacional/1a_liga/Nacional/interior.aspx?content_id=328030|archive-date=31 May 2014}}</ref> On 3 May, he scored twice in a 3–0 away victory against already crowned league champions [[FC Porto]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.record.xl.pt/Futebol/Nacional/1a_liga/Nacional/interior.aspx?content_id=341580|title=Fábio Coentrão: "'Espetar' 3–0 no Dragão é bom"|trans-title=Fábio Coentrão: "'Handing out' 3–0 at the Dragão is good"|newspaper=Record|last=Avelãs|first=Luís|language=pt|date=3 May 2008|access-date=30 May 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140531090526/http://www.record.xl.pt/Futebol/Nacional/1a_liga/Nacional/interior.aspx?content_id=341580|archive-date=31 May 2014}}</ref>

In the summer of 2008, Coentrão transferred to [[Real Zaragoza]], [[2007–08 La Liga|recently relegated]] into Spain's [[Segunda División]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.heraldo.es/noticias/deportes/coentrao_tercer_fichaje.html|title=Coentrao, el tercer fichaje|trans-title=Coentrao, the third signing|newspaper=[[Heraldo de Aragón]]|last=Giménez|first=Paco|language=es|date=18 July 2008|access-date=30 May 2014}}</ref> After almost no appearances during [[2008–09 Segunda División|the campaign]], however,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://futbol.as.com/futbol/2009/01/10/mas_futbol/1231542003_850215.html|title=Coentrao deja de ser jugador del Zaragoza|trans-title=Coentrao is no longer a Zaragoza player|newspaper=[[Diario AS]]|language=es|date=10 January 2009|access-date=30 May 2014}}</ref> he returned to Portugal and Rio Ave in January 2009, still owned by Benfica.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.record.xl.pt/Futebol/Nacional/1a_liga/rio_ave/interior.aspx?content_id=369935|title=Fábio Coentrão confirmado|trans-title=Fábio Coentrão confirmed|newspaper=Record|language=pt|date=5 January 2009|access-date=30 May 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402113552/http://www.record.xl.pt/Futebol/Nacional/1a_liga/rio_ave/interior.aspx?content_id=369935|archive-date=2 April 2015}}</ref> On 15 February he scored following an individual effort, albeit in a 3–1 loss at Porto.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.record.xl.pt/Futebol/Nacional/1a_liga/interior.aspx?content_id=387288|title=FC Porto-Rio Ave, 3–1 (Lucho 37' gp, Farías 86', 89'; Fábio Coentrão 72')|trans-title=FC Porto-Rio Ave, 3–1 (Lucho 37' pk, Farías 86', 89'; Fábio Coentrão 72')|newspaper=Record|language=pt|date=15 February 2009|access-date=30 May 2014}}</ref>

Coentrão extended his contract in late October 2009 until 2015, with a release clause of €30&nbsp;million.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://web3.cmvm.pt/sdi2004/emitentes/docs/FR25728.pdf|title=Comunicado|trans-title=Announcement|publisher=[[Portuguese Securities Market Commission]]|language=pt|date=29 October 2009|access-date=6 July 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120427231026/http://web3.cmvm.pt/sdi2004/emitentes/docs/FR25728.pdf|archive-date=27 April 2012}}</ref> On 2 December, having played some matches as a [[Defender (association football)#Full-back|left-back]], he scored his first goal in [[UEFA|European competition]], against [[FC BATE Borisov]] of [[Belarus]] in a 2–1 away win in the [[2009–10 UEFA Europa League|group stage]] of the [[UEFA Europa League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/01e0-0e7370508614-8ffb0b0e3ca8-1000--bate-run-aground-as-eagles-soar/|title=BATE run aground as Eagles soar|publisher=UEFA|date=2 December 2009|access-date=25 April 2021}}</ref>

On 10 February 2010, Benfica sold 20% of Coentrão's economic rights on any future transfer to a [[Third party ownership in association football|third party owner]], [[Benfica Stars Fund]], along with other teammates. He was tagged at €15&nbsp;million, with the fund paying €3&nbsp;million.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://web3.cmvm.pt/sdi2004/emitentes/docs/FR26903.pdf|title=Comunicado|trans-title=Announcement|publisher=Portuguese Securities Market Commission|language=pt|date=10 February 2010|access-date=5 July 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110928170422/http://web3.cmvm.pt/sdi2004/emitentes/docs/FR26903.pdf|archive-date=28 September 2011}}</ref> During [[2009–10 Primeira Liga|that season]], he had a breakthrough year, appearing in a total of 45 games to win the league and the [[Taça da Liga]];<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.jn.pt/justica/sou-jogador-de-futebol-reformado-disse-fabio-coentrao-em-tribunal-11763211.html/|title="Sou jogador de futebol reformado", disse Fábio Coentrão em tribunal|trans-title="I'm a retired football player", said Fábio Coentrão in court|newspaper=[[Jornal de Notícias]]|language=pt|date=29 January 2020|access-date=13 June 2024}}</ref> for his performances, he was voted [[CNID Awards in football#Portuguese League Breakthrough Player of the Year|Portuguese League Breakthrough Player of the Year]].<ref name=CNID>{{cite web|url=http://www.cnid.pt/index2.php?option=com_content&do_pdf=1&id=128|title=Rosa Mota e Carlos Lopes recebem Prémio Fernando Soromenho|trans-title=Rosa Mota and Carlos Lopes receive Fernando Soromenho Award|publisher=CNID|language=pt|date=25 May 2010|access-date=27 May 2010|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120324185449/http://www.cnid.pt/index2.php?option=com_content&do_pdf=1&id=128|archive-date=24 March 2012}}</ref>

On 27 September 2010, fully established with both his club and the national team, the 22-year-old Coentrão renewed his link until 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://web3.cmvm.pt/sdi2004/emitentes/docs/FR30137.pdf|title=Comunicado|trans-title=Announcement|publisher=Portuguese Securities Market Commission|language=pt|date=27 September 2010|access-date=5 July 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111026002653/http://web3.cmvm.pt/sdi2004/emitentes/docs/FR30137.pdf|archive-date=26 October 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/91/portugal/2010/09/27/2139322/fabio-coentrao-signs-new-deal-at-benfica|title=Fabio Coentrao signs new deal at Benfica|publisher=Goal|last=Coerts|first=Stefan|date=27 September 2010|access-date=28 September 2010}}</ref> On 2 November he scored his first career brace, helping to a 4–3 home defeat of [[Olympique Lyonnais]] in the [[2010–11 UEFA Champions League|group phase]] of the [[UEFA Champions League]] – in a 67-minute fast break, he combined with [[Carlos Martins (footballer)|Carlos Martins]] to make it 4–0 for the hosts.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2002876--benfica-vs-lyon/|title=Coentrão inspires Benfica revival|publisher=UEFA|date=2 November 2010|access-date=17 April 2011|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101105010750/http://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/matches/season%3D2011/round%3D2000118/match%3D2002876/index.html|archive-date=5 November 2010}}</ref>

===Real Madrid===
On 5 July 2011, after extensive negotiations, Benfica and [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] reached an agreement in principle over the transfer of Coentrão, who signed a six-year contract the same day for €30 million<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0254-0d7d29bc632a-c71bdc73adc4-1000--madrid-confirm-coentrao-transfer-from-benfica/|title=Madrid confirm Coentrão transfer from Benfica|publisher=UEFA|date=5 July 2011|access-date=5 July 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://web3.cmvm.pt/sdi2004/emitentes/docs/FR34622.pdf|title=Comunicado|trans-title=Announcement|publisher=Portuguese Securities Market Commission|language=pt|date=5 July 2011|access-date=31 December 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303235547/http://web3.cmvm.pt/sdi2004/emitentes/docs/FR34622.pdf|archive-date=3 March 2016}}</ref>– [[Ezequiel Garay]] went in the other direction as part of the deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://football.uk.reuters.com/leagues/primera/news/2011/07/05/LDE7640X7.php|title=Real Madrid sign fullback Coentrao from Benfica|agency=[[Reuters]]|date=5 July 2011|access-date=13 July 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120710150031/http://football.uk.reuters.com/leagues/primera/news/2011/07/05/LDE7640X7.php|archive-date=10 July 2012}}</ref> He made his debut in a pre-season [[Exhibition game|friendly]] against the [[Los Angeles Galaxy]] on the 16th, creating an [[Assist (association football)|assist]] for [[Karim Benzema]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.neontommy.com/news/2011/07/real-madrid-tops-la-galaxy-4-1-world-football-challenge-opener|title=Real Madrid tops LA Galaxy 4–1 in World Football Challenge opener|publisher=Neon Tommy|date=17 July 2011|access-date=26 December 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141226223622/http://www.neontommy.com/news/2011/07/real-madrid-tops-la-galaxy-4-1-world-football-challenge-opener|archive-date=26 December 2014}}</ref> His first two official games were against [[FC Barcelona]] in the [[Supercopa de España]]: in the first leg, he came on as a [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] for [[Sami Khedira]] in the second half of a 2–2 home draw and played as a [[Midfielder#Defensive midfielder|defensive midfielder]], and he started at left-back in the second match, a [[2011 Supercopa de España|3–2 loss]] at the [[Camp Nou]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://elpais.com/diario/2011/08/20/deportes/1313791202_850215.html|title=Coentrão y el vertigo|trans-title=Coentrão and vertigo|newspaper=[[El País]]|location=Madrid|last=Torres|first=Diego|language=es|date=20 August 2011|access-date=9 October 2015}}</ref>

[[File:Fabio Coentrao.jpg|thumb|Coentrão in action for Real Madrid in the [[2011–12 UEFA Champions League]]]]
Coentrão made his [[La Liga]] debut on 28 August 2011 at former club Zaragoza, appearing as a central midfielder in a 6–0 rout (90 minutes played).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/324018?cc=5739|title=Ronaldo gets Madrid show underway|publisher=[[ESPN FC|ESPN Soccernet]]|date=28 August 2011|access-date=2 September 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121102065146/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/324018?cc=5739|archive-date=2 November 2012}}</ref> While he featured mostly in these positions, he was also deployed by manager [[José Mourinho]] as a right-back, against [[Sporting de Gijón]] on 3 December<ref>[http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=323902&cc=5739 Merengues maintain winning run] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111207022012/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=323902&cc=5739|date=7 December 2011}}; ESPN Soccernet, 3 December 2011</ref> and against Barcelona the following week,<ref>[http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=323887&cc=5739 Barca come back to win Clasico] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120127152402/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=323887&cc=5739|date=27 January 2012}}; ESPN Soccernet, 10 December 2011</ref> [[2011–12 La Liga|winning the league]] in his first year.

In the last minutes of the second matchday in the [[2012–13 La Liga|2012–13 season]], Coentrão was [[Ejection (sports)|sent off]] after insulting [[Referee (association football)|referee]] Pérez Lasa whilst on the substitutes bench, in an eventual 2–1 defeat at [[Getafe CF]]. He subsequently received a four-match ban.<ref>[http://www.goal.com/en-us/news/88/spain/2012/08/29/3338802/coentrao-handed-four-match-ban-misses-supercopa-clasico Coentrao handed four-match ban, misses Supercopa Clasico]; Goal, 29 August 2012</ref>

Coentrão scored his first goal with Real Madrid on 16 December 2012, netting after a [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] pass to help the hosts come from behind against [[RCD Espanyol]], as the game eventually ended 2–2.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espnfc.com/uk/en/report/348363/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=5739|title=Albin denies Madrid at the death|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=16 December 2012|access-date=16 December 2012}}</ref> On 2 September of the following year, [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] launched a late loan bid for him on transfer deadline day. It was accepted by the Spaniards, but the deal fell through when they failed to secure a replacement in [[Guilherme Siqueira]] from [[Granada CF]], who subsequently joined Benfica on loan.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23941584|title=Manchester United: Fabio Coentrao move fails|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=3 September 2013|access-date=3 September 2013}}</ref>

Coentrão started the play that led to [[Gareth Bale]]'s individual effort for the 2–1 winner over Barcelona in [[2014 Copa del Rey final|the final]] of the [[Copa del Rey]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/10771036/Real-Madrid-2-Barcelona-1-Copa-del-Rey-final-report-Gareth-Bale-winner.html|title=Real Madrid 2 Barcelona 1, Copa del Rey final: match report as Gareth Bale scores wonder winner|newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|location=London|last=White|first=Jim|date=17 April 2014|access-date=9 October 2015|url-access=subscription|url-status=live|archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/10771036/Real-Madrid-2-Barcelona-1-Copa-del-Rey-final-report-Gareth-Bale-winner.html|archive-date=12 January 2022}}{{cbignore}}</ref> He also started both legs of the [[2013–14 UEFA Champions League|Champions League semi-final]] against holders [[FC Bayern Munich]] as Real Madrid dismantled the opposition 5–0 on aggregate en route to their tenth European title, ''La Décima''.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/apr/29/bayern-munich-real-madrid-champions-league-match-report|title=Sergio Ramos and Cristiano Ronaldo roll Real Madrid past Bayern Munich|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|last=Hytner|first=David|date=29 April 2014|access-date=9 October 2013}}</ref>

Still under manager [[Carlo Ancelotti]], Coentrão was sparingly played in the [[2014–15 La Liga|2014–15 campaign]] mainly due to injuries,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.elmundo.es/deportes/2015/08/11/55ca3322e2704e2c5f8b4599.html|title=Coentrao, el regreso del hombre ausente|trans-title=Coentrao, the return of the absent man|newspaper=[[El Mundo (Spain)|El Mundo]]|last=Lambea|first=Alberto|language=es|date=11 August 2015|access-date=9 October 2015}}</ref> with only five league starts out of nine appearances. On 26 August 2015, it was announced he was loaned to [[AS Monaco FC]] in a [[2015–16 Ligue 1|season]]-long move.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.asmonaco.com/en/article/coentrao-deal-agreed-68730.html|title=Coentrão deal agreed|publisher=AS Monaco|date=26 August 2015|access-date=26 August 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160415154735/http://www.asmonaco.com/en/article/coentrao-deal-agreed-68730.html|archive-date=15 April 2016|df=dmy-all}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2015/08/official-announcement-coentrao|title=Official announcement: Coentrão|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=26 August 2015|access-date=26 August 2015}}</ref> He made his competitive debut against [[Gazélec Ajaccio]] on 13 September, replacing [[Adama Traoré (footballer, born 28 June 1995)|Adama Traoré]] in an eventual 1–0 away win,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.eurosport.fr/football/ligue-1/2015-2016/face-au-gazelec-ajaccio-monaco-a-eu-chaud-mais-il-regoute-a-la-victoire-1-0_sto4909690/story.shtml|title=Face au Gazélec Ajaccio, Monaco a eu chaud mais il regoûte à la victoire (1–0)|trans-title=Against Gazélec Ajaccio, Monaco sweated but enjoy win (1–0)|publisher=[[Eurosport]]|last=Alard|first=Lucile|language=fr|date=13 September 2015|access-date=24 July 2016}}</ref> and scored his first goal for his new team 11 days later to help the visitors come from behind at [[Montpellier HSC]] to win 3–2.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/montpellier-vs-monaco/report/341632|title=Montpellier 2–3 Monaco: Fabinho's late spot-kick helps seals visitors' comeback|publisher=[[Sky Sports]]|date=24 September 2015|access-date=9 October 2015}}</ref>

As Madrid won the league championship in [[2016–17 La Liga|2016–17]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.laliga.es/noticias/real-madrid-campeon-de-laliga-santander-2016-17|title=El Real Madrid, campeón de LaLiga Santander 2016/17|trans-title=Real Madrid, LaLiga Santander champions 2016/17|publisher=[[La Liga]]|language=es|date=21 May 2017|access-date=22 May 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/39926301|title=Malaga 0–2 Real Madrid|publisher=BBC Sport|date=21 May 2017|access-date=22 May 2017}}</ref> in which Coentrão contributed with just three appearances.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.maisfutebol.iol.pt/made-in/espanha/cada-minuto-de-jogo-de-coentrao-custa-53-mil-euros-ao-real-madrid|title=Cada minuto de jogo de Coentrão custa 53 mil euros ao Real Madrid|trans-title=Every minute of play for Coentrão costs Real Madrid 53 thousand euros|publisher=Mais Futebol|language=pt|date=21 March 2017|access-date=22 May 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.maisfutebol.iol.pt/made-in/internacional/real-madrid-coentrao-titular-cinco-meses-depois|title=Real Madrid: Coentrão titular, cinco meses depois|trans-title=Real Madrid: Five months later, Coentrão starts|publisher=Mais Futebol|language=pt|date=15 April 2017|access-date=22 May 2017}}</ref> He himself admitted not being fit enough to represent the club;<ref>{{cite web|url=https://desporto.sapo.pt/futebol/liga_espanhola/artigo/2017/03/29/fabio-coentrao-nao-estou-em-condicoes-para-jogar-pelo-real-madrid|title=Fábio Coentrão: "Não estou em condições para jogar pelo Real Madrid"|trans-title=Fábio Coentrão: "I am in no condition of playing for Real Madrid"|publisher=SAPO|language=pt|date=29 March 2017|access-date=22 May 2017}}</ref> in [[2016–17 UEFA Champions League|the season's Champions League]] he appeared in two group stage games,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/37839393|title=Legia Warsaw 3–3 Real Madrid|publisher=BBC Sport|date=2 November 2016|access-date=6 June 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/38055041|title=Sporting Lisbon 1–2 Real Madrid|publisher=BBC Sport|date=22 November 2016|access-date=6 June 2017}}</ref> and his team won the competition for the second consecutive time.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0250-0c5117c008df-de0901ea6dae-1000--majestic-real-madrid-win-champions-league-in-cardiff/|title=Majestic Real Madrid win Champions League in Cardiff|publisher=UEFA|last=Haslam|first=Andrew|date=3 June 2017|access-date=4 June 2017}}</ref>

On 5 July 2017, Coentrão was loaned to Sporting in a [[2017–18 Primeira Liga|season]]-long move,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sporting.pt/pt/noticias/clube/comunicados/2017-07-05/comunicado-sporting-clube-de-portugal-futebol-sad|title=Comunicado Sporting Clube de Portugal – Futebol, SAD|trans-title=Sporting Clube de Portugal announcement – Football, PLSC|publisher=Sporting CP|language=pt|date=5 July 2017|access-date=5 July 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2017/07/official-communication-coentrao|title=Official announcement: Coentrão|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=5 July 2017|access-date=5 July 2017}}</ref> despite having stated that in Portugal he would only play for Benfica.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.dn.pt/desporto/benfica/interior/fabio-coentrao-em-portugal-so-jogo-pelo-benfica-4610142.html|title=Fábio Coentrão: "Em Portugal só jogo pelo Benfica"|trans-title=Fábio Coentrão: "In Portugal I only play for Benfica"|newspaper=[[Diário de Notícias]]|language=pt|date=5 June 2015|access-date=5 July 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://rr.sapo.pt/noticia/85551/coentrao_pode_lamentar_ter_dito_que_so_jogaria_no_benfica|title=Coentrão pode lamentar ter dito que só jogaria no Benfica|trans-title=Fábio Coentrão might regret having said that he would only play for Benfica|publisher=[[Rádio Renascença]]|language=pt|date=6 June 2017|access-date=5 July 2017}}</ref>

===Rio Ave return===
After terminating his contract with Real Madrid, Coentrão signed with Rio Ave for [[2018–19 Primeira Liga|one season]] on 31 August 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rioavefc.pt/tenho-de-voltar-ao-clube-da-minha-terra-para-ser-feliz/|title="Tenho de voltar ao clube da minha terra para ser feliz"|trans-title=I have to return to my home club to be happy|publisher=Rio Ave F.C|language=pt|date=31 August 2018|access-date=31 August 2018|url-status=dead|archive-date=4 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181104182055/http://www.rioavefc.pt/tenho-de-voltar-ao-clube-da-minha-terra-para-ser-feliz/}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/08/official-announcement-coentrao|title=Official announcement: Coentrão|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=31 August 2018|access-date=31 August 2018}}</ref> He received 11 yellow cards and two red, was released on 30 June 2019 and did not find a new club for the start of 2019–20.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.goal.com/en-om/news/from-ronaldos-real-madrid-sidekick-to-unemployed-the-demise/15gmbggdtovej1e550g6fypdsp|title=From Ronaldo's Real Madrid sidekick to unemployed – the demise of Fabio Coentrao|publisher=Goal|last=Francis|first=Kieran|date=23 September 2019|access-date=26 September 2019}}</ref>

On 29 January 2020, Coentrão announced his retirement from professional football.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://rr.sapo.pt/2020/01/29/futebol-nacional/fabio-coentrao-anuncia-retirada-do-futebol/noticia/180129/|title=Fábio Coentrão anuncia retirada do futebol|trans-title=Fábio Coentrão announces retirement from football|publisher=Rádio Renascença|language=pt|date=29 January 2020|access-date=29 January 2020}}</ref> In October, however, he agreed to a new one-year deal at the [[Estádio dos Arcos]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.publico.pt/2020/10/06/desporto/noticia/fabio-coentrao-regresso-futebol-rio-ave-1934149|title=Fábio Coentrão de regresso ao futebol e ao Rio Ave|trans-title=Fábio Coentrão returns to football and Rio Ave|newspaper=[[Público (Portugal)|Público]]|language=pt|date=6 October 2020|access-date=7 October 2020}}</ref>

==International career==
[[File:Fabio Coentrao (L), Angel Di Maria (R) – Portugal vs. Argentina, 9th February 2011 (1).jpg|thumb|Coentrão (left) marking [[Ángel Di María]] in a friendly match against [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]] on 9 February 2011]]

An international for [[Portugal national football team|Portugal]] at youth level,<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20070712043453/http://www.uefa.com/competitions/under19/fixturesresults/round=2253/match=85310/report=rp.html Unbeaten Portugal progress in style]; at UEFA</ref> Coentrão was voted MVP in the 2007 Madeira Cup for the [[Portugal national under-20 football team|under-20 team]],<ref>[https://www.fpf.pt/portal/page/portal/PORTAL_FUTEBOL/SELECCOES/NOTICIA?notid=3202380 Sub-20 vencem na Madeira (Under-20s win in Madeira)] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110615172936/http://www.fpf.pt/portal/page/portal/PORTAL_FUTEBOL/SELECCOES/NOTICIA?notid=3202380|date=15 June 2011}}; [[Portuguese Football Federation]], 2 March 2007 (in Portuguese)</ref> also being crowned the competition's top scorer. Subsequently, he represented the nation in the [[2007 FIFA U-20 World Cup]]<ref>{{FIFA player|269784}}</ref> and, two years later, made his [[Portugal national under-21 football team|under-21]] debut, notably [[2009 Toulon Tournament|taking part]] in the [[Toulon Tournament]] and scoring a [[hat-trick]] in the 6–0 group stage rout of [[Qatar national under-20 football team|Qatar]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://maisfutebol.iol.pt/sub-21-portugal-goleia-qatar-6-0-no-adeus-a-toulon|title=Sub-21: Portugal goleia Qatar (6–0) no adeus a Toulon|trans-title=Under-21: Portugal rout Qatar (6–0) in farewell to Toulon|publisher=Mais Futebol|language=pt|date=8 June 2009|access-date=20 September 2019}}</ref>

After consistent performances at Benfica, although he started rarely in the early 2009–10, Coentrão earned his first senior call-up in November 2009, for the decisive [[2010 FIFA World Cup]] [[2010 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA)|qualification playoffs]] against [[Bosnia and Herzegovina national football team|Bosnia and Herzegovina]], and made his debut in the first leg on 14 November at the [[Estádio da Luz]], playing 21 minutes in the 1–0 win.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/world-cup/6576236/Portugal-take-slight-advantage-over-Bosnia-Herzegovina-to-World-Cup-play-off-second-leg.html|title=Portugal take slight advantage over Bosnia-Herzegovina to World Cup play-off second leg|newspaper=The Daily Telegraph|location=London|last=Hoult|first=Nick|date=16 November 2009|access-date=9 October 2015|url-access=subscription|url-status=live|archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/world-cup/6576236/Portugal-take-slight-advantage-over-Bosnia-Herzegovina-to-World-Cup-play-off-second-leg.html|archive-date=12 January 2022}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

Coentrão was chosen for [[Carlos Queiroz]]'s squad of 23 for the final stages, starting as left-back ahead of another adapted player, [[Duda (footballer, born 1980)|Duda]]. He played all the matches in South Africa, in an eventual [[Single-elimination tournament|round of 16]] exit.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.zonalmarking.net/2010/09/03/fifa-2010-technical-report-summary/|title=FIFA's 289-page technical report on the 2010 World Cup – in 15 points|publisher=Zonal Marking|date=3 September 2010|access-date=8 June 2016|url-status=dead|archive-date=4 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181104193726/http://www.zonalmarking.net/2010/09/03/fifa-2010-technical-report-summary/}}</ref>

On 10 August 2011, Coentrão scored his first international goal, netting through a rare header in a 5–0 victory over [[Luxembourg national football team|Luxembourg]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.foxsports.com/soccer/story/portugal-routs-luxembourg-50-in-friendly-42546465-081011|title=Portugal routs Luxembourg 5–0 in friendly|publisher=[[Fox Sports]]|date=10 August 2011|access-date=7 April 2018}}</ref> He played all the games and minutes at [[UEFA Euro 2012]], acting as left-back for the semi-finalists.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/history/news/0252-0cdc4f07099d-bbe9e9886641-1000--spain-survive-test-of-nerve-against-portugal-to-reach-euro-/|title=Spain survive test of nerve to reach final|publisher=UEFA|last=Burke|first=Chris|date=27 June 2012|access-date=8 June 2016}}</ref>

Coentrão suffered an injury in the second half of Portugal's first game at the [[2014 FIFA World Cup|2014 World Cup]], against [[Germany national football team|Germany]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/news/y=2014/m=6/news=german-lessons-for-cr7-s-portugal-2373410.html|title=Muller-inspired Germany thrash ten-man Portugal|publisher=FIFA|date=16 June 2014|access-date=18 June 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140617210838/http://www.fifa.com/worldcup/news/y=2014/m=6/news=german-lessons-for-cr7-s-portugal-2373410.html|archive-date=17 June 2014}}</ref> and was ruled out for the remainder of the tournament.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/jun/17/fabio-coentrao-hugo-almeida-portugal-injured-world-cup|title=Portugal lose Fabio Coentrão and Hugo Almeida for rest of group stage|newspaper=The Guardian|last=Meagher|first=Gerard|date=17 June 2014|access-date=26 June 2014}}</ref> He played a key role in a 2–1 home defeat of [[Serbia national football team|Serbia]] on 29 March 2015, which put them top of the [[UEFA Euro 2016 qualifying|Euro 2016 qualifying group]], crossing for the opening goal by a [[Ricardo Carvalho]] header and then scoring the winner from [[João Moutinho]]'s pass.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro-2020/news/0253-0d7ff0cbb8bf-7677474ee0fd-1000--portugal-see-off-serbia-to-top-group-i/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210425212712/https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro-2020/news/0253-0d7ff0cbb8bf-7677474ee0fd-1000--portugal-see-off-serbia-to-top-group-i/|url-status=dead|archive-date=25 April 2021|title=Portugal see off Serbia to top Group I|publisher=UEFA|date=29 March 2015|access-date=25 April 2021}}</ref>

Coentrão missed [[UEFA Euro 2016|Euro 2016]], which Portugal won, due to a thigh injury, contracted in training with Monaco.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/european-championship/story/2850865/portugal-defender-fabio-coentrao-set-to-miss-euro-2016|title=Monaco, Portugal defender Fabio Coentrao set to miss Euro 2016|publisher=ESPN FC|last=Rodden|first=Mark|date=15 April 2016|access-date=8 June 2016}}</ref> He returned to action after 697 days for a [[2018 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA)|2018 World Cup qualifier]] against [[Hungary national football team|Hungary]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.maisfutebol.iol.pt/portugal/03-09-2017/selecao-o-regresso-de-fabio-coentrao-697-dias-depois#/|title=Seleção: o regresso de Fábio Coentrão, 697 dias depois|trans-title=National team: the return of Fábio Coentrão, 697 days later|publisher=Mais Futebol|language=pt|date=3 September 2017|access-date=3 October 2017}}</ref> but was stretchered off in the first half of an eventual 1–0 win in [[Budapest]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/Hungary-vs-Portugal/350171|title=Hungary 0–1 Portugal|publisher=Sky Sports|date=3 September 2017|access-date=3 October 2017}}</ref>

Coentrão was named in a preliminary 35-man squad for the [[2018 FIFA World Cup|2018 World Cup]] in Russia,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/revealed-every-world-cup-2018-squad-23-man-preliminary-lists/oa0atsduflsv1nsf6oqk576rb|title=Revealed: Every World Cup 2018 squad – 23-man & preliminary lists & when will they be announced?|publisher=Goal|date=17 May 2018|access-date=17 May 2018}}</ref> but he did not make the final cut.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sbs.com.au/news/portugal-world-cup-squad|title=Nearly half Portugal's Euro squad to miss World Cup|publisher=[[Special Broadcasting Service]]|date=17 May 2018|access-date=17 May 2018}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Coentrão's second cousin, [[Rui Coentrão|Rui]], was also a footballer in the same position. He spent most of his career with [[Varzim S.C.|Varzim SC]], and was a youth international.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rtp.pt/noticias/selecao-nacional/rui-coentrao-ja-falamos-sobre-as-coisas-mas-e-boas-que-fizemos_d637865|title=Rui Coentrão: "Já falámos sobre as coisas más e boas que fizemos"|trans-title=Rui Coentrão: "We already spoke about the good and bad things that we did"|publisher=[[Rádio e Televisão de Portugal]]|language=pt|date=22 March 2013|access-date=24 October 2019}}</ref>

After retiring from professional football, Coentrão decided to become a [[Ship-owner|shipowner]] [[fisherman]], following in the footsteps of his father. He told Empower Brands Channel: "Life in the sea is not a shame, as many people think. It is a job like any other. Not only that, the sea is beautiful and we need it. People who love the sea and who want to experience the sea need to follow their dream. It is also a job for the new generations. My father had a boat, he used to fish and I always went with him as a child. My life was the sea... the sea and fishing. Of course, I knew that football would one day end and that I should take a new direction in my life. And my happiness is this boat and this is the life I want to lead."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TjPVnJcXRis|title=Fábio Coentrão é o rosto de uma nova geração de armadores {{!}} Mudar para Melhor|trans-title=Fábio Coentrão is the face of a new generation of shipowners {{!}} Change for the Better|via=[[YouTube]]|language=pt|date=14 December 2021|access-date=3 January 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.ojogo.pt/futebol/noticias/o-pos-carreira-de-coentrao-a-vida-no-mar-nao-e-uma-vergonha-14451574.html|title=O pós-carreira de Coentrão: "A vida no mar não é uma vergonha"|trans-title=Coentrão's post-career: "Sea life is no shame"|newspaper=[[O Jogo]]|language=pt|date=30 December 2021|access-date=7 January 2022}}</ref>
